info.title: KoshSetu — AICTE FDR Portal API
info.description: Prototype API for SIH26265 (Streamline of security deposit / FDR portal). Bank verification is simulated; a simulated result is never independent authentication and never bypasses officer review.

post.description:
Attest and submit.

Requires a clean, parsed document. The submitted snapshot is immutable, so
later changes travel through a correction request instead.

Officer scrutiny.

An acceptance here is an administrative decision recorded against simulated
evidence in this prototype; it is not a real-world authenticity assurance.

Link a successor instrument.

The predecessor keeps its dates, amount, documents and check history; a
replacement never rewrites the original record.

post.description:
Verify the stored object, scan it, then extract fields from a clean file.

Finalizing twice returns the same document rather than creating a second
one, so a retry after a dropped response is safe.
Re-run extraction on a clean document, preserving earlier evidence rows.
Issue a single-document, short-lived read ticket.

get.description:
Stream a document for a valid, unexpired ticket.

The ticket is re-checked against the reader's current scope on every use,
so a revoked role cannot keep reading with an old link.
Fixture catalogue for the demonstration. Officials only.

schema.title: Response List Requests Api V1 Release Requests Get

post.description: Record one bureau's decision. Only its assigned officer may do so.
Maker step: the preparing officer is recorded and cannot later approve.

Final approval.

Everything is re-checked inside the transaction: current authority, the
version the caller saw, every required clearance, the document checklist,
holds and maker/checker separation. The result is an administrative
approval, not a confirmation that a bank released any money.

get.description: Server-derived due windows. A date is never a release approval.

get.description:
Recompute the digest chain.

This demonstrates tamper evidence. It is not a claim of immutability: a
privileged database operator can still alter rows, which is why a
deployment also revokes UPDATE/DELETE and exports signed checkpoints.

post.description:
Run the threshold scan on demand.

A deployment runs this on a schedule (Celery Beat in the brief). Running it
twice cannot create a duplicate logical reminder.

Create the schema and load the synthetic dataset.

Every stage is idempotent and the stages are separately addressable,
because a serverless runtime caps how long one request may take and the
whole load does not always fit. Re-running a stage is always safe:
`seed` skips a populated database, and `findings` only evaluates
instruments that have none yet.

A scheduler calls this; it is idempotent, so a repeated run creates no
duplicate reminder. GET is accepted because some schedulers only issue GET.
